name: Craig Jones Riding Control System
description: A study companion to Craig Jones’s Power Ride, with a control-focused starting point and comparison to Gordon Ryan’s mount-maintenance material.
summary: Use Power Ride to separate leg control, upper-body control and turtle riding when studying why a top position fails to hold.
overview: Power Ride: A New Philosophy on Pinning by Craig Jones organizes top control through lower-body tools, upper-body tools and turtle rides. This guide helps locate the kind of control problem you want to investigate before moving to the course’s submission material.

products.title: Power Ride: A New Philosophy on Pinning
products.blurb: Use Power Ride to separate leg control, upper-body control and turtle riding when studying why a top position fails to hold.
products.best_for: You reach top position but cannot identify which part of your control breaks first.
products.study_focus: Use Standard Operating Procedure to orient the study, then connect an entry in Volume 5 with a control topic in Volumes 2–3.

guide.display_title: Craig Jones: Riding Control with Power Ride

fits: You reach top position but cannot identify which part of your control breaks first.
consider_alternative_if: For a study anchored specifically to mounted position and remounting, compare Gordon Ryan’s mount course.

includes: Separate volumes on leg control and upper-body tools.
Turtle rides and entries from side control, mount and passing positions.
A final volume connecting control topics to submission topics.
limits: The curriculum ranges across several rides and pins; it is broader than a mount-only maintenance study.

start_here.title: Compare what each control section is trying to explain
start_here.task: Read the free Volume 2 and Volume 3 contents beside a note about one top position you recently lost. Mark whether your unanswered question concerns the legs, upper body, or both. Then locate the matching entry position in Volume 5. With course access, begin with Standard Operating Procedure before combining those sections.
